fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` re-exports 7 names it does not define, each marked
`# noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)` — 3 from `._processors_identity`
(`_rederive_keyring_keys`, `process_key_event`, `process_signature`) and 4 from
`._processors_status` (`_fold_claimed_session`, `_fold_close_metadata`,
`_fold_plan_review_phase`, `process_status`). ADR 0111 forbids internal shims.

Censused on `origin/main` at `50d5a36539d` by parsing every `.py` under `src`, `tests`
and `scripts` with `ast`, resolving relative imports, and separately scanning
`ast.Attribute` and string constants:

- **4 names have zero importers** and can be deleted outright: `_fold_claimed_session`,
  `_fold_close_metadata`, `_fold_plan_review_phase`, `_rederive_keyring_keys`. None is
  used inside `_processors.py` either, so they are dead in both directions.
- `process_key_event` — 1 importer, production: `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:19`.
- `process_signature` — 5 sites: `_replay.py:19` plus
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15`, and `tests/unit/test_signing.py`
  at both `:117` and `:133`.
- `process_status` — 6 sites: `_replay.py:19` plus
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`, `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`, and
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`.
- No attribute-style access (`_processors.process_status(...)`) anywhere.
- Two string constants contain `rebar.reducer._processors`; both were read and neither
  needs editing. See Out of scope.

A line-oriented grep for `from rebar.reducer._processors import <name>` reports 0
importers for `process_key_event` and misses `test_attestations_reducer.py` entirely,
because `_replay.py` and that test import inside multi-line parenthesized statements
where the name sits on its own line. The AST census above is the correct instrument;
the grep count is not.

**`docs/event-schema.md` names 2 of the moving symbols in a shape no code census can
see.** It locates each processor as a bare filename plus symbol —
`_processors.py process_status` at `:234` and `_processors.py _fold_claimed_session` at
`:249` — rather than as a dotted import path, so a census keyed on
`rebar.reducer._processors` matches neither. Both lines become wrong the moment the
re-exports are deleted, and `:82` already shows the convention the file uses elsewhere:
`reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_close_metadata`.

## Change

1. Repoint the 3 names that have importers to the modules that define them:
   `process_key_event` and `process_signature` to `rebar.reducer._processors_identity`,
   `process_status` to `rebar.reducer._processors_status`.
2. **Four** importers pull a genuine `_processors` member on the same statement, so they
   must be split rather than rewritten wholesale:
   - `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:19` imports 18 names, of which 3 move — and they come
     from two different siblings, so this becomes **three** statements: 15 names stay on
     `_processors`, `process_key_event` and `process_signature` go to
     `_processors_identity`, `process_status` to `_processors_status`.
   - `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13` imports `attestation_kind`,
     `process_signature`, `process_snapshot`, `process_status` — likewise **three**
     statements: `attestation_kind` and `process_snapshot` stay, `process_signature`
     moves to `_processors_identity`, `process_status` to `_processors_status`.
   - `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15` and
     `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10` each also import
     `process_snapshot`, defined in `_processors.py` at `:469`, which stays — two
     statements each.
3. Delete all 7 re-exports from `_processors.py`. The whole
   `from ._processors_status import (...)` statement goes, since all 4 of its names are
   re-export-only. The `._processors_identity` statement keeps
   `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (used at `:139`, `:520`), `_fold_author_attribution`
   (`:81`, `:185`, `:296`) and `attestation_kind` (`:508`), which carry no `noqa`
   because `_processors.py` uses them.
4. Extend the held-out oracle `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, which
   already covers `_processors`/`_processors_status` and sets the convention: assert the
   re-exports are absent AND that the canonical modules still expose them, so the
   assertion cannot pass vacuously.
5. Add a `docs/release-notes.md` entry naming the 3 import paths that moved
   (`process_key_event`, `process_signature`, `process_status` are no longer importable
   from `rebar.reducer._processors`) and the module that now owns each.
6. Correct the 2 stale locators in `docs/event-schema.md`: `:234` to
   `reducer/_processors_status.py:process_status` and `:249` to
   `reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_claimed_session`, matching `:82`'s existing form.

## Testing

- A case in `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py` asserting
  `not hasattr(_processors, name)` for all 7 names, paired with positive assertions that
  `_processors_identity` and `_processors_status` still expose them.
- The repointed test modules must stay green unchanged in substance — only their import
  lines move.
- `make verify` covers the whole-tree effect, including the reducer replay suites that
  exercise `_replay.py`'s dispatch, which is the one production consumer.
- The 2 doc locators are verified by resolving each corrected `path:symbol` pair against
  the tree, not by eye.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `grep -cF 're-exported for back-compat' src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
      prints 0.
- [ ] **AC2** Re-running the AST census reports 0 importers for all 7 names.
- [ ] **AC3** `python -c "from rebar.reducer import _processors as p; assert not any(hasattr(p, n) for n in ['_rederive_keyring_keys','process_key_event','process_signature','_fold_claimed_session','_fold_close_metadata','_fold_plan_review_phase','process_status'])"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **AC4** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors_identity import process_key_event, process_signature; from rebar.reducer._processors_status import process_status"`
      exits 0, proving the moved names stay reachable at their canonical modules.
- [ ] **AC5** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors import process_snapshot, attestation_kind"`
      exits 0, proving the two names that stay on `_processors` are unaffected.
- [ ] **AC6** `ruff check src tests` exits 0 with no output.
- [ ] **AC7** `pytest tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] **AC8** That file's collected case count is strictly greater than its count on
      `origin/main`, measured with `pytest --collect-only -q` on both.
- [ ] **AC9** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly 12 paths:
      `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py`, the 7 named
      test modules, `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`,
      `docs/release-notes.md`, and `docs/event-schema.md`.
- [ ] **AC10** `docs/release-notes.md` gains an entry naming all 3 moved import paths,
      and the file's only diff is additions.
- [ ] **AC11** `grep -cF '_processors.py process_status' docs/event-schema.md` prints 0,
      and `grep -cF '_processors.py _fold_claimed_session' docs/event-schema.md` prints 0.
- [ ] **AC12** `git grep -nF '_processors' docs/event-schema.md` returns no line naming a
      symbol that `python -c "import importlib; ..."` cannot resolve at the module the
      line names — checked for every `_processors*` locator in the file, so the fix is
      proven by resolution rather than by string match.
- [ ] **AC13** `make verify` exits 0.

## Ordering

Independent of the resolver-shim stories `insanitary-divine-moa` and
`peckish-marmatite-cuckoo` — different modules, no shared source file. May land in any
order relative to them.

## Out of scope — checked, not merely unexamined

- **`docs/event-schema.md:256`, which names `_processors.py _clear_claimed_session`.**
  That locator is already wrong on `origin/main`, independently of this change:
  `_clear_claimed_session` is defined at `_processors_status.py:35` and has never been
  re-exported from `_processors.py`. It is a pre-existing documentation defect, not
  breakage this slice introduces, and AC12 is scoped to locators this change can
  falsify. Tracked separately.
- `attestation_kind`, which 5 files import from `_processors`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py:45`, `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:354` and
  `:437`, `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:176`, `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`).
  It is **not** a re-export: `_processors.py` uses it itself at `:508`, so its import
  stays and carries no `noqa`. Repointing those 5 importers is a separate judgement call,
  not part of removing re-exports.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:63`, which captures logs on the logger
  named `"rebar.reducer._processors"`. That record is emitted at `_processors.py:495`
  inside `process_snapshot`, under that module's own `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, and
  `process_snapshot` stays — so the string remains correct and must not be changed.
- `src/rebar/reconciler/_field_contract.py:114`, whose `notes=` prose names
  `rebar.reducer._processors.process_tag_delta`. That function is defined in
  `_processors.py` at `:434` and stays, so the prose stays accurate.
- The `_engine_support/resolver.py` shim, tracked on `insanitary-divine-moa`.
- Any behavior change in the processors themselves.
